scope.problem: Six RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests two-process tests spawned children inside a TemporaryDirectory and only called Process.join(timeout=5) before letting the with-block exit. join returns whether or not the child ended, so under CI load a still-running child writing into the temp worktree makes rmtree raise OSError [Errno 39] Directory not empty on cleanup. The failure lands on whichever branch happened to be running at that moment.
cited_failures: task/OPS-ANTIGRAVITY-SHARED-ACCOUNT-001, GitHub Actions run 35182030826 (failed twice, including an explicit re-run)
scope.fix: Added RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests._reap(*processes, timeout=5) which joins, then escalates to terminate() and finally kill() (each followed by a join) until every child is provably dead, and replaced the bare join(timeout=5) calls in the six affected tests' teardown with calls to _reap. No test assertion changed; only teardown changed. The one test that already checked is_alive was left alone.
scope.new_test_added: test_reap_terminates_a_child_that_outlives_its_join_timeout: spawns a child that sleeps 120s, calls _reap(process, timeout=1), and asserts the child is dead (is_alive() is False, exitcode is not None) after reaping.

verified_behavior: Process.join(timeout=...) alone does not prove a child has exited
_reap escalates join -> terminate+join -> kill+join until the child is confirmed dead
A child that ignores its join deadline is dead after _reap runs
The six affected two-process tests still pass their original assertions unchanged
The full .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py suite remains green after the teardown change
promotion_boundary: Source and isolated-test scope only. No hosted deployment and no live runtime state edit.
